# MC2T player-test kit

*Generated by `tools/mc2t_kit.py` from the game's data. Answers use the game's own rule: each support number is `round half up (base x room multiplier x question multiplier)`; guard, drawing and gaffes are never scaled.*

## 0. Quick reference

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Participants | 5 per round, 3 rounds (RITE): fix top issues between rounds |
| Segments | New-to-genre, deckbuilder-literate, politics-literate (at least 1 each); phone in portrait, own thumb |
| Session | Cold start, 15 min think-aloud play, 3 freeze probes, 6 predict-then-reveal items, 8 term definitions, debrief |
| Question multipliers | strong 1.3, weak 0.7 |
| Promised-answer rule | A card's printed numbers are base values; the room and the question change Gain and Opponent; Guard, Draw and Gaffe do not scale |

## 1. Predict-then-reveal items (criteria C2, K2)

Show the card face and the room's Details panel. Ask: *'If you play this now, what changes?'* Record each number the participant gives, then play it and compare. Score **1 = all numbers right, 0.5 = direction right but a number wrong, 0 = wrong direction or cannot say.**

## 2. SAGAT freeze probes (criterion C1)

Freeze the screen (cover it or pause), then ask. Ground truth comes from the engine state at the freeze; the facilitator reads it off the Details panel.

| # | When | Ask | Ground truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Turn 2 of the first battle | What will the opponent do next turn? | The intent line, if shown; 'unknown' only if the card that reveals it was not played |
| F2 | After a gaffe | How close are you to losing because of gaffes? | Gaffe meter value against the stage's gaffe limit (Details) |
| F3 | Mid-battle | What do you need to win, and how far away are you? | Support bar value against the threshold; turns left |
| F4 | After a card with Guard | What does Guard do and how much do you have? | Guard banks up to the cap (rules.json `guard_cap`); it absorbs the opponent's next attack |
| F5 | In the Office | What would happen if you start a 31-hour level with 2 hours left in the week? | The level cannot start (a level must end within the work week) |

## 3. Term definitions (criterion C4)

Ask: *'In your own words, what does ___ mean in this game?'* Score 1 correct, 0.5 partly, 0 wrong. Ground truth in the right column comes from `design/GAME_SYSTEMS.md`.

| Term | Meaning in this game |
|---|---|
| Threshold | The support number you must reach to win the stage |
| Gaffe meter | Fills with mistakes; when full you lose the stage |
| Guard | A bank (cap 5) that blocks the opponent's next attack |
| Standing | How much one organization or party trusts you; unlocks backings, requests and votes |
| Backing | A perk an organization lends you for a stage or a level; gated by standing |
| Constituency support | One of four meta numbers; at 15 or below a Town Hall is forced |
| Party support | One of four meta numbers; at 0 funding freezes |
| Legislative Work | Bills you carried and the laws they became |

## 4. Coherence probes (criteria K1 to K5)

| # | Probe | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | Sort 12 UI words into 'same thing' groups (card sort); give the participant: Guard, Block, Gaffe, Standing, Support, Backing, Booster, Level, Stage, Room, Threshold, Member | Participants group Backing with Booster; the designer decides whether they should (see report finding L1) |
| K2 | Predict items P1 to P12 above | Median 0.5 or more (gate), 80% target |
| K3 | After a lost stage: 'Why did you lose?' | Participant names the true cause (gaffe meter, turn limit, support at zero) from the result panel alone |
| K4 | After a delayed consequence (a promise, a vote, decay): 'What caused this?' | Participant traces it to their own earlier choice |
| K5 | Teach-back: 'Explain to a friend how a turn works in 60 seconds' | Mentions energy, hand, a question, the opponent's reply |

## 5. Mobile probes (criteria MO1 to MO7)

| # | Task | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| MO1 | Play one battle one-handed (thumb) in portrait | Count mis-taps (a tap that hits a neighbouring control); target under 3 percent of taps; gate over 10 percent |
| MO2 | Read a card at arm's length | Can the participant read the cost and numbers without zooming? |
| MO5 | Lock the phone mid-stage for one minute, then return | Is the stage still where they left it? (Known gap: nothing saves mid-stage; see report) |
| MO6 | Rotate or switch to another app and back | No lost state, no layout break |
